notice: Illustrative operation/network component sensitivities, NOT a current regional quote, full TCO, measured performance, or prediction of latency/availability. 30 days; no discounts/free tier. Request counts are explicit scenario assumptions; omitted components are not zero in a real deployment.

source_notes: https://aws.amazon.com/s3/pricing/ supplies request/transfer rules and examples, not a machine-verified complete regional rate table here.
https://aws.amazon.com/vpc/pricing/ supplies the Ohio USD 0.045/GB NAT example.
https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/optimizing-data-transfer-costs-when-using-aws-network-load-balancer/ documents combined USD 0.02/GB for the example cross-AZ edge.
https://aws.amazon.com/kms/pricing/ supplies symmetric-request examples. Application KMS and storage SSE requests must be counted separately.
Each traffic edge declares its own billing byte unit. These examples use 2^30; production SKUs must supply their actual unit, endpoints, payers, region and storage class.

scenarios.assumptions: 10000 dirty shard streams/s, one payload and one root PUT-like request each. Excludes keys, pages, catalog, reads, retries, storage, compute and network.
100 payload packs/s, but still 10000 shard-root updates/s. Shows why packing alone does not remove metadata cost.

100 qualified compatible commit domains/s; each pays payload, commit root and two additional metadata/envelope PUTs, plus one application wrap. Conditional design scenario, not a proved grouping result; incompatible keys or more pages add cost.
Idle data-plane request component is zero. Shared membership/control jobs, durable storage and compute still have their own costs.
One metadata check per idle shard per minute. Counts API invocations even when no data changes. Illustrates a floor to avoid.

Two directed remote follower payload copies of 10 MiB/s input. Rates are already summed at the two endpoints, not doubled again as a round trip. Excludes acknowledgements, clients, search replicas, catch-up and voter disks/compute.

Ohio-example per-byte processing rate. Does not include NAT hours, cross-AZ hops, storage, requests or compute. A gateway endpoint removes this modeled processing component only when the actual route supports it.
